title: Position plan source
description: plans/<id>.json, schema 1.3 (1.0, without label_offset, 1.1, without the document, the storey and the section of v0.114, and 1.2, without the plan type, the load symbols and the load transfer levels of v0.116, are read as they are) -- one position plan as Woodcore saves it, the source calc/domains/plan.py exports from (docs/domain/position-plans.md §3.3sexies). Written by Woodcore only. Coordinates are in the units of the sheet the plan is drawn on -- points for a PDF, pixels for an image, viewBox units for an SVG -- from its top left corner, y down; angles in degrees, clockwise on the drawing from its right. Since v0.99 an element and an axis may carry a `style` of their own, a factor over the plan's three: optional and additive -- absent means «follows the plan» -- so schema_version is deliberately NOT bumped for it and no file needs migrating.

schema_version.description: -- accepted: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7; an older one is read as it is, every field it lacks being optional. 1.4 (v0.117): a column (S) or a point Auflager (M) may carry its `angle`, and an element its own `show_length`. 1.5 (issue #9): a plan carries its `dimensions`. 1.6 (issue #18): a plan carries its construction aids, `aids`. 1.7 (issue #43): a plan carries its `texts`, which Woodcore writes only where a text is placed.

plan_type.description: The plan's type (v0.116, Woodcore's «Type de plan»): a floor plan («coupe en plan»), an elevation section («coupe en élévation», whose role is section) or a load-path plan («plan de descente de charges», STE Compact 02 pp. 14-15: a floor plan that also carries the six load symbols, types PL and LL). Optional (1.3): absent, derived from `role` -- a section, else a floor plan.

group.description: The folder Woodcore files this source in, "" or absent at the root. A FIELD and never a directory: the ids stay flat, so the rule that the id is the file name is untouched and no show-* call changes (calc/tools/grouped_list.py). Optional and additive -- a file written before it existed reads as the root -- so schema_version is deliberately NOT bumped for it.

superposition.description: Another plan of the same tab shown over this one in Woodcore's window (v0.116, the «Superposition» module) -- a drawing aid, never printed and never exported: what lies on the storey above or below while this one is drawn. The other plan's point q is shown at s·q + offset, s this plan's units per metre over the other's where both have a scale (else 1). Optional and additive, so schema_version does not move for it; a plan named that no longer exists is shown as nothing, never refused.

plan.description: The id of the plan shown over this one -- a plan of the same tab, never this one.

elements.description: Whether its drawn elements are shown with its background (default true).

opacity.description: How opaque the superposed plan is, 0.05 to 1 (default 0.5).

colour.description: Its background as it is (normal), in grey or in one of five colours (default red).

tint_elements.description: Whether its elements take that colour too (default false: they keep their own).

offset.description: [dx, dy] in this plan's sheet units: where the other plan's origin lands, set by «Aligner» (two clicks). Absent: the two crops' top left corners on each other.

name.description: What the engineer calls this object, free text (Woodcore's «Nom»). Its ID is composed of it until the ID is written over (calc/tools/identity.py). Optional and additive: a source without one is named by its ID alone.

id.description: The plan's id: its file name, and the string the report addresses it by (show-plan("EG")).

label.description: Woodcore's «Description»: free text, printed in the figure's caption; may be empty.

floor.description: The floor's character, the second of its positions' numbers (U, 0, 1, ...) -- used to number a new element; may be empty.

storey.description: The storey the plan shows, in free text of any length (EG, 2.UG, Mezzanine) -- offered from plan.STOREYS in the window's language; `floor` is the one character of its positions' numbers, proposed from it (plan.storey_floor). Optional (1.2): absent, empty.

role.description: A floor plan, whose positions it locates, or a section, which shows the storeys (its storey lines and boxes). Optional (1.2): absent, a floor plan.

section_plan.description: The id of the section plan a floor plan refers to, whose box of this plan's storey a sheet highlights. Optional (1.2).

sheet.description: The size of the sheet the plan is drawn on, in its units: the background's, or an empty A3 page in points.

background.description: The architect's plan the symbols are drawn over. Absent for a plan drawn on an empty sheet.

file.description: Its path relative to the project folder, with forward slashes (01_Pläne/03_Pavillon.pdf); a .pdf, .png, .jpg or .svg inside the folder. A .dxf or .dwg through its document only.

page.description: The page of a PDF, from 1; 1 for an image or an SVG.

sha256.description: The file's SHA-256 when the plan was saved: the export warns when the file has changed since.

opacity.description: How much of the background shows through the white veil under the symbols, 0 to 1.

document.description: The document of plans/documents/ the plan is drawn on (calc/domains/plan_documents.py): its file and page are then kept in step with it here, so a plan still reads where the document is gone. Optional (1.2): absent, the plan is drawn on `file` directly, as before.

crop.description: The part of the sheet the report shows. Absent: the whole sheet.

scale.description: How long a metre of the building is on the sheet: 'ratio' (1:n, for a PDF, whose points are paper) or 'calibration' (two points and the real length between them). Absent: no scale, and so no lengths.

show_lengths.description: Whether the lengths in metres are written beside the walls, the beams and each side of the slabs (V, H, W, T, D; the walls alone until v0.117) -- an element's own `show_length` overriding it; needs a scale.

style.description: The three sliders: factors on the strokes, on the symbols placed on a point, and on the texts, from 0.25 to 3. An element and an axis may state a factor of their own over these (their own `style`); a factor this object does not name is refused (calc/domains/figure_style.py).

axes.description: The plan's axes: a line through a point at an angle, drawn across the frame the report shows, with a bubble at one end, both or neither.

label.description: A letter for a vertical axis, a number for a horizontal one, by convention.

angle.description: 90 for a vertical axis, 0 for a horizontal one, anything else for an oblique one.

style.description: This axis's own factors, MULTIPLYING the plan's three, from 0.25 to 3 -- a factor and never a size, so it means the same whatever frame the plan is drawn at. An axis accepts `line` (its dash-dot line) and `text` (the bubble its name is set in, whose radius is a text size); `point` is refused, an axis placing no symbol on a point. Absent, or a factor left out of it: that factor follows the plan. Optional and additive; schema_version does not move for it.

elements.description: The STE symbols, in the order they were drawn.

type.description: V, H, W, T, S, A, D, Ö, B, M or L -- or, on a load-path plan only (1.3), PL (a point load) or LL (a line load).

subtype.description: D: scheibe or normal; M: vert, horiz or vh; L: linie or punkt; B: wand or decke; PL and LL: vert, horiz or vh. Absent for the other types.

label.description: The position number, a position id of the project; empty for an opening or a concrete wall. A load symbol's number (PL, LL) is the plan's own -- Pxxx, Lxxx -- and no position.

angle.description: In degrees, clockwise on the drawing from its right; absent: 0. A point load's horizontal direction (1.3); a column's (S) or a point Auflager's (M) turn about its centre, its square drawn turned (1.4). Refused on any other element.

show_length.description: Whether this element's length is written beside it -- a wall's, a beam's, each side of a slab's (V, H, W, T, D) --, whatever the plan's `show_lengths` says; absent: as the plan says (1.4). Needs a scale.

span.description: A slab's span direction, in degrees; absent for its short side.

diagonal.description: Which diagonal a slab without diaphragm action shows, 0 or 1.

label_offset.description: [dx, dy], how far the position number was moved by hand from its own place (the middle of a line, the centre of an area, above a point), in sheet units; absent where it was not. Only on an element that carries a number.

style.description: This element's own factors, MULTIPLYING the plan's three, from 0.25 to 3 -- a factor and never a size, so it means the same whatever frame the plan is drawn at. An element accepts all three: `line` (a wall's, a beam's, a slab's outline and its diagonals), `point` (a column's square, an Auflager's, an Abfangung's mark) and `text` (its position number, its box, a wall's length). Absent, or a factor left out of it: that factor follows the plan. Optional and additive; schema_version does not move for it.

storey_lines.description: A section's storey lines, each a storey's level drawn across the section between two points, in sheet units: the overlay draws it dash-dot with the storey in a bubble at both ends. Only on a section (role 'section').

storey.description: The storey the line marks, as the floor plans name it.

storey_boxes.description: A section's storey boxes, each the part of the section a storey takes up, {x, y, w, h} in sheet units: not drawn in the overlay -- a sheet highlights the box of the storey its floor plan shows. Only on a section.

floor.description: The storey's numbering character, which its STE designation x1xx is made of (1.3); absent: proposed from the storey (plan.storey_floor).

dimensions.description: The plan's dimensions (source 1.5, issue #9): `kind` horizontal, vertical, parallel (two points), chain (three or more, `axis` one of the three) or angle (the corner, then a point on each side); `points` in sheet units -- points of the sheet, not references, so a dimension does not follow an element moved --, `offset` the line's distance from the middle of its ends (an angle's: the arc's radius, negative for the reflex), and a `style` of `line` and `text`. The value is never stored: it is computed from the points and the plan's scale.

load_levels.description: A section's load transfer levels (1.3, STE Compact 02 p. 14, «Niveau de reprise des charges»): each a red dash-dot line between two points, in sheet units, with a red arrow coming down onto each end and «Niveau de reprise des charges (x0xx)» beside it. Only on a section.

storey.description: The storey whose numbering character makes its designation.

floor.description: That numbering character; absent: proposed from the storey.

label_offset.description: [dx, dy], how far its words were moved by hand from their own place, in sheet units.

aids.description: The plan's construction aids (source 1.6, issue #18): lines without ends the plan is laid out with in Woodcore, drawn and snapped to there and never in the report nor on a sheet. Each is stored resolved, as an axis without bubbles -- `point` in sheet units and `angle` in degrees clockwise from the right, within (-90, 90] --, `kind` saying only how it was made: horizontal, vertical, through two points, or parallel to another line at a distance.

texts.description: The texts placed with the Text tool (issue #43, calc/domains/figure_text.py): each centred on its one point. Written only by a source that holds one, whose schema_version says so.

id.description: A fire-protection plan's text's id (fire-source holds the same list); a position plan's texts have none, as its other entries.

points.description: Its centre on the sheet, in sheet units: one point, as every entry of a plan is moved and turned by its points.

text.description: What is printed, a line per line: `{1}` is a token, where the variable `vars["1"]` is printed; a literal brace is written twice, `{{` and `}}`. A token naming no variable is a defect of the file (D-13). An underscore makes a subscript, as in every label of a figure.

vars.description: The variables the tokens name, by token: a link to a variable of the export, its `show` and its `last` value.

origin.description: 'formulas' for a domain of the «Formules» tab, whose id is `instance`; absent for the export.

show.description: How it is printed (D-09): 'value', its value and unit; 'symbol', its symbol, '=', its value and unit.

last.description: What the variable gave when Woodcore's window last saved (D-14), printed where it can no longer be read, with a warning (D-06).

style.description: The factor this text states over the drawing's: `text` only (figure_style.ENTRY_KEYS).
